episodes.158705: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a weak frontal boundary that was nearly stationary across southwest, to east central Minnesota, and over adjacent west central Wisconsin.  Modest instability and enough wind shear allowed for a couple robust storms to develop along this front. One developed near Redwood Falls and dropped quarter size hail in southern Renville County, north of Franklin. Similar thunderstorm cores  that produced quarter size hail near Franklin moved southward into eastern Redwood County but no reports of hail were received. A similar storm developed in the northern suburbs of the Twin Cities and produced quarter size hail.
episodes.158718: A broader midlevel trough moved across western Colorado and acted on ample residual monsoonal moisture to produce numerous showers and thunderstorms across the area. Some storms produced heavy rain which led to localized debris flows across portions of the Grizzly Creek Fire burn scar.
episodes.158729: A mid-level disturbance moved into a increasingly unstable air mass as it moved from the eastern Adirondacks into western VT and then the Connecticut River Valley. A thunderstorm developed in eastern NY and gradually increased in intensity as it moved across Vermont, then intensified rapidly just prior to moving into NH. A brief wet microburst in Hartford, VT knocked down several trees on several streets that caused power outage to more than 1000 customers.
episodes.158739: Widespread severe thunderstorms formed during the afternoon and evening within an environment of moderate CAPE and moderate shear. A shortwave moved across the Ohio Valley giving support for multiple rounds of convection, primarily in the form of multicell clusters and linear segments. Although damaging winds were the main impact, a few storms also created large hail.  Flash flooding was reported from slow moving thunderstorms in Lycoming and Tioga Counties.
episodes.158754: Several rounds of thunderstorms developed across northeast Wisconsin during the afternoon and evening hours.  The strongest storms produced hail up to ping pong size, damaging wind gusts, along with heavy rain and flash flooding.  Portions of east-central Wisconsin received 2 to 5 inches of rain through the overnight hours. Lightning struck a hour in Kiel, causing a fire, as well as a pole in Green Bay, which damaged 2 garages.
episodes.158755: Strong thunderstorms produced gusty winds as they tracked over the Lake Michigan nearshore waters during the afternoon hours.
episodes.158792: An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 60 mph just east of Biddle.
episodes.158858: A disturbance crossing New Mexico on July 14, 2021, brought ample moisture, instability, and lift to allow for an uptick in storm coverage across northern and central New Mexico. Widespread showers and thunderstorms developed by the afternoon hours, and with a very active start to the monsoon season and daily rounds of heavy rain, soils were primed for additional flash flooding. Strong thunderstorms and heavy rain particularly impacted Jaconita and Pojoaque in Santa Fe County where flooding and mud flow forced the closures of several roads. A truck became stuck in the flood waters near Jaconita, but fortunately, no injuries occurred.
episodes.158899: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to northern Monmouth County on the evening of July 14.  Rainfall amounts of 1.5 to 2.5 inches fell in a short amount of time.
episodes.159013: A cold front produced numerous thunderstorms that resulted in scattered wind damage across east-central Virginia into southern Maryland.
episodes.159016: A cold front produced numerous thunderstorms that resulted in scattered wind damage across east-central Virginia into southern Maryland.
episodes.159018: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms produced numerous instances of gusty winds over the tidal Potomac River and portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.159046: A line of strong to severe storms moved across south-central Wisconsin during the mid to late afternoon hours on July 14th, 2021.
episodes.159055: A mid-level trough moved across the mid-Atlantic on July 14. A weak surface trough was also present. This caused a few thunderstorms to develop in an unstable but weakly sheared environment. A couple of cells briefly became severe and produced a few instances of damaging wind. Storms were also slow moving, with heavy rain proving to be a greater threat than severe weather. Storm coverage waned by the mid evening hours.
episodes.159090: Severe thunderstorms across portions of Laramie and Albany Counties produced hailstones up to golf ball and lime size respectively. A home owner noted hail broke one of their windows near Federal.
episodes.159340: A severe thunderstorm developed along the Wyoming-Montana border in far northeastern Campbell County and tracked east-southeast across northern Crook County. The storm produced small hail and wind gusts around 60 mph.
episodes.159341: A severe thunderstorm developed over west central Campbell County and tracked east-southeast into southwest Crook County before weakening. The storm produced large hail and wind gusts over 70 mph.
episodes.159408: During the afternoon on July 14th, several strong thunderstorms affected the Lake Michigan nearshore waters producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.159428: Severe thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon and evening of Wednesday, July 14.  Some of the storms produced damaging winds and numerous tornadoes.  Brief torrential rainfall was also observed with the stronger storm cells.  The areas that were hit hardest were in Buchanan, Delaware, Benton, Linn, and Jones counties in IA, where a total of 14 tornadoes occurred.  7 of the tornadoes had no visible damage.
episodes.159670: An isolated thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust just east of Biddle.
episodes.159781: Heavy rain producing thunderstorms moved across Banner and Scotts Bluff Counties producing over an inch of rainfall contributing to street flooding in the city of Scottsbluff and out in the country of Banner County.
episodes.160025: Areas of thunderstorms moved across the Sandhills and southwest Nebraska the late night of July 13, producing large hail in Lincoln County.
episodes.160267: Lake Erie remained in the warm sector as a surface low moved from central Lake Michigan to near northern Georgian Bay during the early afternoon through early evening of the 13th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front moved eastward and dissipated, allowing the residual surface trough axis to near the western end of Lake Erie by early evening. Multiple squall lines moved eastward over and near Lake Erie, and produced gale-force peak wind gusts at several locations along the Ohio shore. These storms encountered moderate instability and DCAPE, and marginally-moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.160378: A line of severe thunderstorms tracked southeast across the Black Hills, producing wind gusts to 70 mph across portions of the area.
episodes.160396: A microburst struck Indian River Campground southeast of Steuben in Schoolcraft County on the afternoon of the 14th.  Over 50 trees were snapped or uprooted over a 300 x 200 yard area.  Maximum wind speeds were estimated at 85 mph.  Fortunately, all of the campsites were empty at the time of the storm.
episodes.160397: Thunderstorms training over northern Menominee County caused flash flooding from Cunard to Hermansville on the afternoon of the 14th.  Portions of the Hermanville Golf Course were under water from the storms.
episodes.160441: A weakening ridge of high pressure extended from the Maine and New Hampshire coast southeast to Rhode Island. At the same time, a surface warm front was beginning to advance northward. This combined with rising temperatures and very humid air created scattered strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.160746: Warm and moist tropical air was present over Central New York when a quasi-stationary warm front slowly moved through the region. These conditions provided supported for severe thunderstorms with damaging winds resulting in numerous reports of trees and wires knocked down. A wind gust of nearly 70 kts was also measured by a mesonet station.
episodes.160825: A surface low pressure system was centered over Kansas and Nebraska with attendant warm front draped across north central Iowa. This was bisected by an outflow boundary from morning convection across western Iowa. As morning activity exited the are the atmosphere quickly recovered steep low and mid level lapse rates exceeded 8 C/km with 0-6 km shear over 40 knots. Near the remnant outflow boundary 0-1 km SRH exceeded 150 m2/s2. Storms developed along this boundary and moved east along the warm front, spawning a number of tornadoes across the state. In fact, this is in the top 5 for tornadoes occurring in a single day for the state of Iowa since reliable records began in the 1980s. By evening convection congealed into an MCS, bringing heavy rain to portions of the state. A line of training storms set up north of the Des Moines metro, resulting in localized flash flooding.
episodes.160826: Warm and moist tropical air was present over Northeastern Pennsylvania when a quasi-stationary warm front slowly moved through the region. These conditions provided support for one storm to become severe with damaging winds, knocking down a tree onto a roadway.
episodes.160843: A small line of thunderstorms moved slowly northeast across parts of northeast Iowa during the early morning of July 14th. These storms briefly became strong enough to produce quarter sized hail in Maynard (Fayette County).
episodes.160849: Two tornadoes skipped across portions of northeast Iowa during the late afternoon of July 14th. The first tornado impacted areas between Rockford (Floyd County) and Rudd (Floyd County) and to the east before dissipating northwest of Charles City (Floyd County). The most extensive damage occurred to a hog containment building near the end of its path. This tornado was rated an EF-1. The second tornado caused damage in Oelwein (Fayette County) and locations southwest of the city. This tornado ripped an air handler unit off a restaurant and caused damage at the high school football stadium. This tornado was rated an EF-0. The Governor of Iowa issued a disaster proclamation that included Fayette County.
episodes.160869: Slow-moving thunderstorms trained over Rensselaer County during the afternoon of the 14th, resulting in a bullseye of 2-5 of rainfall over two to three hours over central and southern portions of the county. The runoff from the rainfall washed out or destroyed numerous roads and bridges, some of which would take weeks to months to reconstruct. Damages to roads and bridges totaled around $3 million, according to county officials. The Rensselaer County Executive declared a state of emergency and urged no unnecessary travel after the storms. Governor Hochul requested a Physical Disaster Declaration from the Small Business Administration, citing major damage to 18 homes and 9 businesses totaling $1.895 million, and minor damage to 281 homes and 14 businesses totaling $2.3 million. Some flash flooding extended into the northern portion of Columbia County as well. Some of the storms also produced wind damage with reports of trees and wires down.
episodes.160879: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in a few wind damage reports and flash flooding in southern VT on Wednesday July 14, 2021.
episodes.161140: A decaying MCS that initiated over the Great Plains trekked over Lake Michigan, producing wind gusts in excess of 40 mph along the Manistee county shoreline.
episodes.161227: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
episodes.161247: Scattered severe thunderstorms associated with a surface trough of low pressure produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia and the Virginia Northern Neck.
episodes.161371: A stationary boundary along with a weak area of low pressure triggered a severe thunderstorm across Northeastern New Jersey.
episodes.161388: Monsoon moisture slowly seeped into the region under the big dome of high pressure which was causing record-breaking temperatures, fueling isolated to scattered thunderstorms. As the moisture increased, the main thunderstorm impact transitioned from high winds to flash flooding.
episodes.161389: Monsoon moisture slowly seeped into the region under the big dome of high pressure which was causing record-breaking temperatures, fueling isolated to scattered thunderstorms. As the moisture increased, the main thunderstorm impact transitioned from high winds to flash flooding.
episodes.161456: A weak shortwave trough moving across the state aided in the development of showers and thunderstorms across south-central Arizona on the morning of the 14th. With anomalously high amounts of moisture in place, showers and thunderstorms produced locally heavy rainfall which led to some flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported in northern Pinal County near Florence where Maricopa County Flood Control gages recorded over 1.50 of rainfall. Flash flooding was also reported in the Globe area as heavy rainfall over the recent Telegraph burn scar led to enhanced runoff in Pinal Creek. No injuries or damage were reported.
episodes.161583: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across eastern Pinal and Pima counties during the early morning hours. Flash flooding occurred in northern and western parts of the Tucson Metro area. Lightning also started a small house fire.
episodes.161704: An isolated pulse thunderstorm produced a brief gale-force wind gust along the reef offshore Ocean Reef.
episodes.161750: A slight risk for severe thunderstorms was outlooked for all of our area with very unstable conditions to the south of a warm front and ahead of a shortwave impulse lifting out of Ohio. CAPE values were running 1500-2000 J/kg, and shear values were running 20-25 knots in the west to 30-40 knots in the east. Wind damage and tropical downpours ended up the main hazards as wet bulb zero heights were over 14,000 feet. Severe thunderstorms were observed across much of the area and the adjoining Great Lakes waters.
episodes.161752: Thunderstorms with heavy rain developed between 2 AM and 4 AM in an area of stronger convergence off Lake Erie in southern Erie County. Automated gauges from weather underground were helpful to get ground truth rainfall reports. Repeated heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in the Southern Tier. Multiple road closures were reported. Areal flooding lingered after the flash flood. The heaviest rain hit the headwaters of the east and west branches of Cazenovia Creek, resulting in very high flows into the early afternoon. The gage EBZN6 quickly rose over 6 feet to around 9 feet in just two hours.
episodes.161754: A very moist air mass was in place on the 14th of July with dewpoint temperatures around 70 degrees. As a disturbance aloft moved toward New England, thunderstorms developed over western New Hampshire, with a few being severe.
episodes.161818: Moisture and thunderstorms increased over northern Arizona with several reports of flash flooding.
episodes.161840: A band of showers and thunderstorms developed during the early evening in a moist and unstable environment. The band produced heavy rain across potions of the western Piedmont of central North Carolina during the early evening hours, resulting in isolated flash flooding and isolated wind damage in Randolph County.
episodes.161873: An upper level ridge moved across the northern high plains with mid level northwest flow ahead of it. Moderate instability across much of western Kansas but with weak large scale ascent values with a leeside trough sparking a number of storms out of eastern Colorado. Coupled with moderate shear around 30-35 kts and relatively steep lapse rates, isolated storms pushed across western counties near the Colorado border.
episodes.161919: Deep monsoon moisture continued across northern Arizona with several flash floods.

This was the first and strongest tornado of the day.  It developed west southwest of Lake City and produced tree and power line damage.  The tornado moved into and across the southern portion of Lake City.  Imagery from UAV's and chasers show that the tornado was multi-vortex as it passed through the city.  Up to EF2 damage occurred as it passed through town.  As the tornado moved east of the town, it began to consolidate into a larger funnel and strengthen.  It passed through a farmstead producing considerable damage to the farmhouse and out buildings with EF3 damage noted on the house.  The tornado continued for a few more miles and impacted a confinement facility before lifting to the northwest of Lohrville.  Fortunately, no injuries or deaths occurred with this tornado.

Tornado developed southwest of Shell Rock and moved along 250th Street.  The tornado impacted several farmsteads along 250th producing EF1 damage to buildings and trees at many of the locations.  The tornado was also quite wide with the the max width extending over 600 yards.  The tornado continued into Bremer county.

The tornado moved into Bremer county from Butler county.  The tornado impacted a couple of acreages just east of the county line producing EF0 and EF1 damage before weakening and becoming an intermittent funnel.  The tornado destroyed 2 barns just north of the 4th street SW exit off of Highway 218.  It then crossed the Cedar River just southwest Waverly doing damage to houses on both sides of the river, mostly EF0 and EF1 damage.  After crossing Hilton Avenue, it intensified and produced EF2 damage with extensive tree damage along with toppling a high voltage power line.  The tornado continued farther east and slowly weakened, staying mostly in open rural land.  The tornado eventually lifted to the northwest of Denver.
In Amherst, half dollar sized hail was reported.

The tornado developed and moved to the east, mostly across open agricultural fields.  It did blow down a grain bin on a farmstead and with some minor tree damage as well.  The tornado then began to move southeast continuing to remain in open cropland.  One final farmstead was impacted with some tree damage before the tornado lifted.

An EF0 tornado developed southwest of Oelwein and moved northeast into the city before dissipating. The tornado damaged the ticket booth, fencing and ripped metal siding off of stands at the high school football field. The tornado also blew out the sides of a greenhouse, tipped over the FFA's chicken coop and lifted but did not remove the roof on the main portion of the high school. At a restaurant, an air handler unit was ripped off and windows broken. Some crop and tree damage was noted southwest of the city as well.
